PRIOR FINDINGS AND CURRENT REVIEW BRIEF: Read H016-batch-smoothness.md in FULL, its provenance and retained Bernstein primary sources as relevant, plus H014-disposition.md and H014-independent-review.md. H014 has now passed independent review as an exact enumeration primitive, not a factorer. H017 just supplied a conditional root-geometry supply obstruction and is under a separate review. H018 separately reviews the fixed-degree model/linear candidate. Do not duplicate their supply or enumeration work.

H016's new constructive project claims require independent assessment:
1. For S signed integer pairs of w bits, base construction plus all smooth parts and FULL sparse prime exponent vectors cost (B+S)poly(n), provided w, logB, logS and record widths are poly(n). Retain explicit aggregate bit mass otherwise. Prime generation via sieve or sequential composite marks + sorting is charged. No unit cost on product-tree aggregate integers; fast multiplication is essential.
2. Recognition: Z=product primes<=B, remainder tree computes Z mod x for every |x|>=2; e=ceil(log2 bitlength x), e modular squarings gives Z^(2^e) mod x; gcd is entire B-smooth part. Zero excluded, signs/units/repeats and failed candidates retained. Indexed Bernstein text had a material cutoff mistranscription; source PDF says 2^(2^e)>=x.
3. Full exponent recovery: balanced prime-partition tree repeatedly computes left-prime smooth parts of tagged smooth fragments, passes left and right quotient. At every level fragment bit mass <=2U and disjoint prime-group bit mass P, so another logarithmic factor, not B*S. Leaves p^e decode e via repeated squaring and greedy division by p^(2^j), not e separate divisions. Audit tagging, prime/exponent output widths, data movement, memory and batching amortization (batch bits >=prime-product bits).
4. Explicit costs O(b_total L^3 loglog b_total) arithmetic and looser O(B log³B + b_total L^4 loglog b_total + (I+1)log²(I+b_total+2)) with identifiers/access. Check polynomial and near-linear claims separately; do not attribute a different algorithm's sharp theorem to an unsupported implementation. No executable or finite benchmark was run.

5. IDEAL stage: monic irreducible f, Delta=disc(f), primitive quadratic g and nonzero norm. Reject row if gcd(norm,Delta)>1. For remaining support primes p, gcd(f mod p,g mod p) has degree<=2 and is squarefree. Split to monic factors h. Labels (p,h) are maximal-order primes since p does not divide disc(f), without a global integral basis. Norm exponent alone is insufficient; example f=X³+2X²+X+5,g=X²+1, disc=-655, norm9, one degree-2 ideal with odd valuation1.
Expected polynomial splitting via quadratic Cantor-Zassenhaus (p2 separately); deterministic alternative precomputes every root of f mod p by enumeration for all p<=B at B² poly(n), storing <=d roots/p. Both costs paid; deterministic option fits assumed 2b envelope but says nothing about other randomized stages.
6. Hensel valuations: for h irreducible modp of degree r=1/2 and complement C1 coprime, lift monic f=H_j C_j modp^j to k=E+1, E=v_p(norm). D=(f-HC)/p^j modp, U=(C1^-1 D) modh, V=(D-C1U)/h in Fp[X], update H+p^jU,C+p^jV. Then reduce g modulo H_k; minimum p-adic valuation of remainder coefficients equals ideal valuation in the unramified local extension. Check precision sufficiency, degree drops, repeated roots of g, primes dividing its leading coefficient, widths, and norm sum sum deg(h)*v_h=E. At most w support primes, two ideals/support, each local computation poly(n). Verify canonical sorting/labels and memory. Degree-2 ideal norm may exceed B; cutoff is rational p<=B as Card C explicitly says.
7. Exceptional-row rejection avoids factoring Delta but may destroy supply; must remain an unquantified loss. Character evaluation at supplied good ideals is cheap, but obtaining sufficient characters, rank, algebraic square roots, denominator handling and splitting probability remain unpaid/unproved. Good-prime ideals do not certify algebraic squares. No all-input success theorem.

Independently accept/revise/reject each integer/ideal/cost claim and conditional envelope: H²+B+S per integer stream, plus expected S poly(n) or deterministic (B²+S) good-ideal work; 1.89 remains only conditional on sufficient actual good-prime useful rows, joint smoothness and completion. Original S*B cost was an upper implementation cost, not a lower bound. Do not turn removal of that bottleneck into factoring improvement.
